correctness.rationale: For \(R=\mathbb Z_2[\zeta]/(\zeta^2+\zeta+1)\), the Fermat cubic is smooth because the partial derivatives are \(3x_i^2\). Characteristic-two polarization forces every plane to be a maximal Hermitian isotropic \(\mathbb F_4\)-linear three-subspace; Frobenius-four descent and a \(693\cdot45\cdot3/(5\cdot21)=891\) polar-space count establish completeness. Even-weight splitting and the Singleton bound give 405 pairing codes; the remaining 486 are monomial images of the hexacode. All special tangent maps have rank nine. At the lifted hexacode the exact cubic restriction is \(4(u^3+v^3+w^3)+18uvw\), and the \(uvw\) coefficient survives modulo four under all deformations, obstructing each extra plane. Formal elimination of nine equations yields completed local rings \(R\) for pairing planes and \(R/(2)\) for hexacode planes. Properness and quasi-finiteness give the complete finite scheme decomposition; executable finite checks supplement rather than replace geometric proofs.

value.rationale: A complete relative Fano scheme of planes is a canonical invariant of the smooth Fermat cubic fourfold model. Identifying 405 etale horizontal sections plus 486 reduced vertical points and their first-order obstruction gives a geometrically meaningful complete nonflat degeneration; the exact local rings and orbit incidence clarify why the char-two polar-space configuration is larger than the char-zero extremal configuration. Not a routine normalization or arbitrary slice.
